strings/parse#

Strict readings of numbers and truth values written as text.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

Number("42").int();             // 42
Number("ff").int(16);           // 255
Number("0x2A").int(0);          // base 0 reads the 0b, 0o and 0x prefixes
Number("11111111").byte(2);     // byte 255
Number("6/8").rat().string();   // "3/4"
Number("-42.5").float();        // -42.5
Truth("true").bool();           // true

Description#

Strict readings of numbers and truth values written as text. Nothing is trimmed and a leading + is never accepted.

Explicit bases span 2..36. A rational is an integer or numerator/positive-denominator. Errors keep the exact source text.

Public API#

object Number#

object Number

A number written as text, read as the type asked for.

Number.Number#

Number(origin is string)

A number written as text; nothing is read until asked.

Number.int#

int(base is int = 10) is int

The text as an int in base: 2 to 36, 10 unless told, or 0 to read a 0x, 0o or 0b prefix; InvalidInteger when it is not one.

Number.float#

float() is float

A dotted spelling is read by the runtime, nearest float (#170); one without a dot is an integer, so "-0" stays 0.0 as before.

Number.rat#

rat() is rat

The text as an exact rat: 1.25 or 5/4; InvalidRational otherwise.

Number.byte#

byte(base is int = 10) is byte

Digits below the base, no sign, at most 255; base 0 reads the 0b, 0o and 0x prefixes (#170: the integer reader, not a digit at a time).

object Truth#

object Truth

A truth value written as text: exactly "true" or "false".

Truth.Truth#

Truth(origin is string)

A truth value written as text.

Truth.bool#

bool() is bool

true for exactly "true", false for exactly "false"; InvalidBoolean otherwise.
